title: Corrected BMP canonical exactness
question: Do documented BMP corrections restore the project contract on the frozen fixture and common real data?
hypothesis: All 96 synthetic attempts and both 25-query real-data representations match canonical scores and IDs.
motivation: Resolve native failures before exact external comparisons.
declared_changes: numeric original-ID canonical heap and equal-bound retention
zero-score eligibility and k capped at corpus size
sorted wide bounds replace 16-bit buckets; prefetch/lookahead removed
input_manifest: runs will pin the unchanged fixture, original GSP, prepared queries, split, generated CIFF and exported query hashes
query_split: synthetic fixture plus first 25 calibration queries; held-out unused
timing_boundary: correctness only; no repeated latency comparison
correctness_rule: All ordered IDs and integer scores must match; fixture CIFF unchanged; real GSP round trip byte-identical; no held-out queries or performance claims.
measurement_and_analysis_plan: Execute Rust regressions, same 96-case matrix, then 100K/25-query raw/compressed top-10 agreement.
success_rule: Zero crashes and zero canonical score/ordered-ID mismatches.
failure_rule: Retain and explain every failure; correct and separately review a new code iteration before rerunning.
next_if_negative: Preserve failed artifacts, isolate counterexample and revise patch with explicit deltas.
